Register an exact R type for an Arrow type

Source: R/registry.R
arrow_register.Rd

A typed package, such as 'zuint', 'decimal' or 'zutempo', tells zuarrow which R class is the exact form of an Arrow type. It does so in its .onLoad(), when zuarrow is installed; the registration lasts for the session and is removed when that package unloads.

Usage

arrow_register(
  key,
  to = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  class = NULL,
  package = NULL,
  exact = TRUE
)

arrow_unregister(key)

arrow_registry()

Arguments

key

A format string, a prefix pattern or an extension name.

to

NULL, or a function of (array, schema) returning an R vector.

from

NULL, or a function of (x) returning an array handle.

class

The R classes from handles.

package

The registering package, so its registrations are removed when it unloads.

exact

Whether the conversion is exact.

Value

arrow_register() and arrow_unregister() return key invisibly. arrow_registry() returns a data frame with columns key, kind, class, package and exact.

Details

The key is one of:

  • an Arrow format string, matched exactly: "l" for int64;

  • a prefix pattern ending in * for parameterised types: "d:*" for every decimal, "tsn:*" for every nanosecond timestamp;

  • an extension name, such as "r.decimal", which takes precedence over the storage type's key.

to converts Arrow to R: a function of (array, schema), the column's array and schema handles, returning an R vector of the array's length. It may be implemented in C against nanoarrow's r.h layout. It is called once per batch, and the pieces are combined with c().

from converts R to Arrow: a function of (x) returning an array handle, used for every object that inherits from class.

Inside to, arrow_to_r() on the same column uses the built-in conversion, so a handler can start from it.

A registration declares whether it is exact. One that is not is used only under lossy = "warn" or "allow", and may not replace a type whose built-in conversion is exact. Registering a key again replaces the earlier registration, with a message naming both packages.

Registered handlers apply to the top-level columns of a data frame and to the fields of nested data frames, at any depth, not to the items of a list column. A field under a null row of its data frame is NA.

Examples

arrow_register(
  "l",
  to = function(array, schema) arrow_to_r(array, to = character()),
  exact = TRUE
)
arrow_registry()
#>   key   kind class package exact
#> 1   l format          <NA>  TRUE
arrow_unregister("l")
